intro: I've spent three summers working as a software intern: two at Greenman Pedersen (GPI) and one at TTM Technologies. Here's what I did at each.

jobs.summary: My second summer at GPI, this time on the AI side. Most of what I built helps people use a small local AI on traffic signal data without having to trust it blindly.
highlights: Built a filter assistant that turns plain English into database filters, which people check before anything runs (JavaScript, Fastify, PostgreSQL, Ollama).
Wrote a test harness that ran the same 200 prompts across 8 local models, then picked and tuned a 3B model that fit on a 4 GB GPU.
Prototyped a tool that reads, sorts and names scanned signal records for a 300,000-page digitization project, with a person approving every file.
Made tools that find and fix messy records left over from an old DOS system, with dry runs and a person signing off on every change.

jobs.role: Application Development Intern, GIS & Computer Vision
jobs.summary: My first summer at GPI. Most of it went into a road sign survey: finding signs in video and working out exactly where each one is on a map.
highlights: Used YOLO-E to find signs in survey video, then stereo vision, tracking and GPS to place each sign on the map.
Connected my Python code to the team's existing C# app through a small TCP server, and helped with field testing.
Built a tool for sorting and grouping GIS intersection data, and a multi-user Flask app for checking results and making a QA summary PDF.
Tested a virtual tunnel inspection app built in Unity and wrote up the bugs I found.

jobs.summary: My first real software job, at a defense contractor. I learned how cybersecurity compliance reporting works and then automated the slowest part of it.
highlights: Learned the NIST Risk Management Framework and the DISA tools used to check systems against it.
Built Python and Tkinter apps that let the cybersecurity team update checklist XML files safely, with a review step before anything changes.
Tested them with lots of odd inputs to find the edge cases. The tools were used for five quarterly reports.

details: Coursework: Software Development and Problem Solving I and II, Personal Software Engineering, Engineering Software Systems, Engineering Web-based Software Systems, Discrete Math, Calculus I and II, Statistics
